［#33］
Second, we consistently observed that winning tickets generated on larger, more complex datasets generalized *substantially better* than those generated on small datasets. This is particularly noticeable for winning tickets generated on the ImageNet and Places365 source datasets, which demonstrated competitive performance across all datasets. Interestingly, this effect was not merely a result of training set size, but also appeared to be impacted by the number of classes. This is most clearly exemplified by the differing performance of winning tickets generated on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, both of which feature 50,000 total training examples, but differ in the number of classes. Consistently, CIFAR-100 tickets generalized better than CIFAR-10 tickets, even to simple datasets such as Fashion- MNIST and SVHN, suggesting that simply increasing the number of classes while keeping the dataset

［#35］
Figure 3: Transferring VGG19 winning tickets across datasets. Winning ticket performance on target datasets: SVHN (a), Fashion-MNIST (b), CIFAR-10 (c), CIFAR-100 (d), ImageNet (e), and Places365 (f). Within each plot, each line represents a different source dataset for the winning ticket. In cases where the y-axis has been narrowed to make small differences visible, full y-axes are provided as insets. Error bars represent mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds.

claims.A: winning tickets generated on larger, more complex datasets
claims.B: winning tickets generated on small datasets
claims.S: transferring VGG19 winning tickets across datasets
claims.U: mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds
claims.content: Under transferring VGG19 winning tickets across datasets, comparing winning tickets generated on larger, more complex datasets with winning tickets generated on small datasets on generalization performance on target datasets showed that the larger-dataset tickets had substantially better generalization; uncertainty: mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds.

claims.A: winning tickets generated on the ImageNet and Places365 source datasets
claims.S: transferring VGG19 winning tickets across datasets
claims.U: mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds
claims.content: Under transferring VGG19 winning tickets across datasets, winning tickets generated on the ImageNet and Places365 source datasets on performance across all target datasets showed competitive performance; uncertainty: mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds.

claims.M: generalization performance on target datasets, including Fashion-MNIST and SVHN
claims.S: transferring VGG19 winning tickets from CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 source datasets, both with 50,000 training examples but differing in number of classes
claims.U: mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds
claims.content: Under transferring VGG19 winning tickets from CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 source datasets, both with 50,000 training examples but differing in number of classes, comparing CIFAR-100 winning tickets with CIFAR-10 winning tickets on generalization performance on target datasets, including Fashion-MNIST and SVHN, showed better (CIFAR-100 outperformed CIFAR-10); uncertainty: mean ± standard deviation across six random seeds.
